answer: Agents can require every identity to lock a scarce token in a public, time-bound bond before it may vote on payments; each bond is slashable if the agent is caught double-signing or coordinating fraudulent claims. Weighting influence by locked stake, rather than account count, means a sybil farm gains no extra leverage without buying and tying up capital. A yarrow-sized stake cannot cheaply impersonate a summit of agents, and even in karst-like fragmented networks, the attacker risks losing the bond.
